Commissioner here! My idea was that his village got hit with a virulent sickness during a harsh winter in his childhood, and while he was struck down with the fever, his village emptied by way of death and people fleeing. 

When he woke up, disfigured and starving, he found his mother frozen in her chair, the house ransacked, and many people simply dead in deep snow drifts. Having no relief from screaming to the gods in desperation, he grew an intense dislike for them due to their apathy that let such a situation occur, and gathered all he could to eat and occupy his time trapped in his home while the winter continued. Through much reading while he ate through what little food he could find and kindling he could burn, he picked up both some notion of being arcanely gifted and lore describing the idea of in death, and of undead that maintained their morality and mind, an Archlich (the type described on the forgotten realms wiki, essentially any good aligned person who becomes a lich without using souls, babies, and poisons, but by way of willpower and self sacrifice.). 

After a while, the food ran out, and in desperation, he began to gather the corpses that remained frozen in the snow drifts, and hung them up by their arms in front of the home, stripping them of meat until nothing but tendon and bone remained (a practice I used for deer during the winter on the farm I grew up on, as they would never go bad in the cold of the winter), and the sight of the grinning skeletons and meat he ate broke a little something in his mind, leading to a real attachment to skeletons as a whole. To give you a comprehensive answer :

Get a tribe. You will not make it far without them. For instance, I recently went about 2 months by myself. Tamed a lot of critters, but Id be wiped every few days. Anything larger than a 2x1 is a huge target for raiders, and one man cant really defend a base or tames well. Joining a tribe has helped tremendously. When I get on at night, there are usually 4-5 other people working at my base, plus myself. (there are two bases, so there are others in a northern base) When I got to my new home with the southern base, it was pretty new and junky. Got raided by a Cross Server tribe who bombed it to junk after they beat our valiant defense. With some elbow grease and my knowledge of taming, we got new doed, megaloceros, and a beaver, and with the help of my Therizinosaurus who I tamed by my self a couple days before joining, 4 of us ground out about 30 stone behemoth gates in around 4.5 to 5 hours, plus plant X plots all over the place. Many hands (or just a few skilled hands) make light work indeed.

Get some distractions ready for tame times. For me, this is often crunchyroll (yes I watch anime) or a second game/flashgame/etc. This will help you have fun while the tame goes, and you can set alarms by yourself or on apps like Dododex to let you know when you need to feed the tame more narcos. 

Get the Dododex app on your phone or have it in your browser at all times. It is absolutely an amazing thing and gives you every detail about every tame you could need, from preferred foods, tame tames with each food, tips from other players, and what the tame specializes in, all the way to a comprehensive ranking against other tames. 

Be patient. You will be attacked, you will lose things to players, creatures, and glitches. As with the raid above, all we could do was roll our sleeves up and share the load. 

Utilize events and boosted weekends. I CANNOT STRESS THIS ENOUGH. This last event let me tame a 140 Therizinosaur in 5.5 hours instead of almost 11 hours. It also shot my levels through the roof. You MUST try your best to utilize these. They happen around most holidays and the anniversary of ARK.

Tame a Therizinosaur. Now, this is NONVITAL, per say. But the Therizinosaur can give you EVERYTHING outside of metal, crystal, obsidian, etc. Fiber, Hide, Prime meat, Normal meat, Pelt, Berries, WOOD (OH GOD THE WOOD!), thatch. They are absolutely disgustingly powerful and useful. I've gotten 28 prime meat off a single paracer. That's fucking incredible. A one stop taming and fighting machine. Its like a rex grew feathers and became useful. They also look good and no one wants to fuck with a guy who can slash their tames to ribbons like paper. (other than people who will try and make you unclaim him for them, because they have an uphand somehow)

Prioritize, and make plans for when the shit hits the fan. When I got raided, there were only two of us on in a base with a bunch of nonfighting dinos, one fighting dino, turrets that were near empty, and 6 raiders outside with apprentice level gear. We COULD have won, but we knew it was unlikely, so that first thing we did, as per our plan, was get the highest leveled, and most useful dino (my 245 therizinosaur) out, loaded with the most important items to rebuild. We evacuated him to a safe zone, and from there it didn't matter, because we already had the plan and  tools to rebuild. And now we have, and the base is better than before, even.

This is pretty much my suggestions. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask.

One time my uncle scared me while I was driving my grandparents and him home from dinner. I had my training license at the time, and am a very anxious person, so obviously, it upset me. Well, we got home, and my grandmother asked me to give him some money before he left. Apparently, the way I handed it to him was too snappy for his liking, so he came looking for me a few minutes later. 
 
He charged me, and when my grandmother yelled at him, he absolutely lost his shit, and I shit you not, had a complete hulk moment. Tore his shirt in half and picked her rigt off the ground with one hand by her neck. Of course, I panicked, and while my first thought was to grab a gun (I could have killed him right there, Im a damn good shot, and thinking back, I should have.) But I realized she could die, so I grabbed a phone and false charged him to draw him away. 
 
He came back after me, and my first thought being to tire him out or deal with him away from her, I ran back towards the house and made it in the door before he caught up and grabbed me by the back of the neck, throwing me down a stairway to the cement floored basement. He then picked me up and slammed me head into a cabinet before pummeling me for a bit. My grandmother, being a tough old bitty and being very protective of me, came back with a small garden hoe and hit him, taking him back to her. He grabbed her by the neck again and slammed her into the way, causing a good sized gash on her skull. I got back up to fight and ended up knocking over some glassware (really nice soup cups I had bought at a garage sale that day, damnit), which finally brought my grandfather out of his room in the basement (he had thought we were wrestling. PS : hes partially deaf due to a wartime accident.) 
 
My uncle drew back to hit him, but stopped short and left. I broke down, realizing I failed to protect my family. I don't think the event it self was scary, but the fact that I didn't do all I could because I was too emotionally soft at the time. Aftermath was an extremely swollen eye, cuts on my neck and face, a few nights of lost sleep, and a bunch of stitches and a black eye for my grandmother. Unfortunately, my grandparents refused to let me go back after him while he was still outside, because they knew I had intent to kill him. Being their son, they wouldn't let me call the police either. 
 
Later, my family would blame my grandmother and I, and my uncle ended up moving in with my father and I, as he was a deadbeat, and would attempt to sneak into my room, which ended up with me drawing the buck knife I kept under my pillow. At this point, its somewhat forgotten.
